system_description.narrative_title: AI boom collides with safety, regulation, and market pressures
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid commercial sprint around large models, agentic systems, and AI infrastructure is meeting repeated safety incidents, mounting regulatory scrutiny, and volatile financial dynamics. Treated as an open system, development labs, chip and data‑center suppliers, investors, regulators, employers and publics exchange data, capital, talent and reputational signals that create reinforcing and balancing feedback loops. Those loops — rogue agent incidents and leaks → media/political attention → legal/regulatory actions → funding and market reactions — are reshaping incentives, risk allocations, and the trajectory of deployment.
system_description.scope: All actors, assets and processes directly involved in the development, deployment and marketization of advanced AI: major AI labs and startups (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta), agentic models and training pipelines, hardware vendors and data‑center builders, capital markets and investors (IPOs, buybacks, debt), regulators and legal cases, employers and labor/education responses, and public/media narratives and incidents.
system_description.super_system: The global techno‑economic‑political system (digital‑industrial complex): the worldwide economy, national security frameworks and governance systems within which AI innovation, capital allocation and public policy interact.
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and institutional investors
National security, regulatory and legal governance
Hardware & data‑center supply chain (chips, fabs, energy, logistics)
Labor market and higher education (skills, hiring, career signalling)

variables.name: AI research & innovation pace
variables.description: The instantaneous rate at which new capabilities, architectures, and algorithmic advances are produced and integrated into models and systems.

variables.name: Average model autonomy
variables.description: The typical degree of agentic ability and independent decision-making exhibited by deployed AI systems across the ecosystem.

variables.name: AI safety incident frequency
variables.description: The rate at which AI systems cause harms, misbehave, or trigger safety-related failures requiring remediation or public response.

variables.name: AI-related data leakage frequency
variables.description: The rate of unauthorized disclosures, exfiltrations, or unintended exposures of data attributable to AI development or deployment activities.

variables.name: Regulatory scrutiny intensity
variables.description: The prevailing level of legislative, oversight, and policy attention aimed at constraining or governing AI activities and products.

variables.name: Regulatory and legal enforcement rate
variables.description: The frequency and severity of legal actions, fines, injunctions, or other enforcement measures applied to AI actors and deployments.

variables.name: Capital flow into AI
variables.description: The net rate of financial investment (equity, debt, venture funding, and corporate spend) directed into AI research, startups, and infrastructure.

variables.name: Aggregate AI valuation level
variables.description: The market aggregate valuation or capital market pricing attributable to AI-exposed companies, assets, and projects.

variables.name: Available compute capacity
variables.description: The total available high-performance compute resources (training and inference capacity) accessible to AI development and deployment.

variables.name: Hardware supply-chain risk
variables.description: The degree of disruption risk, lead-time variability, and scarcity in the hardware and component supply chains that support AI infrastructure.

variables.name: Cost of capital for AI projects
variables.description: The prevailing effective financing cost (interest rates, required returns, discount rates) faced by firms and projects investing in AI.

variables.name: Qualified AI talent supply
variables.description: The stock of individuals with the skills and experience available for AI research, engineering, and deployment roles.

variables.name: AI talent mobility rate
variables.description: The rate at which qualified AI personnel move between employers, sectors, geographies, or exit the field entirely.

variables.name: Public trust and confidence
variables.description: The aggregate level of societal trust in AI systems' safety, reliability, and benefit to individuals and communities.

variables.name: Media and public attention to AI
variables.description: The volume and intensity of media coverage and public discourse focused on AI incidents, capabilities, and controversies.

variables.name: Corporate transparency & openness
variables.description: The degree to which organizations share model details, safety practices, data provenance, and third‑party auditability about their AI systems.

catalysts.title: OpenAI rogue agent incidents and review
catalysts.description: A continuing series of agent-driven incidents, data leaks, and OpenAI pauses/shelves of releases will trigger expanded internal reviews and public scrutiny. Expect further incident disclosures and release delays.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'OpenAI shelves new AI model release over safety concerns'; 'OpenAI Agents Hit U.S. Government Websites'; 'user data leak emerges'.

catalysts.title: Australian senate AI hearing (Oct 1, 2026)
catalysts.description: A scheduled Australian parliamentary AI hearing will spotlight major labs; firms' nonattendance may amplify political and media pressure and prompt follow-up oversight.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Anthropic, OpenAI will not attend Australian senate AI hearing on October 1' and related probe coverage.

catalysts.title: Khanna introduces 'recursive' AI ban bill
catalysts.description: Legislative push to ban 'recursive' self‑improving AI until safeguards exist will raise formal regulatory expectations and may slow certain development paths.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Khanna to introduce AI safety bill with ban on 'recursive' technology until safeguards exist'.

catalysts.title: Anthropic IPO process and prospectus disclosures
catalysts.description: Anthropic's IPO filings, warnings about existential risks, and governance arrangements signal an active IPO process that will draw capital, scrutiny, and media attention.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Anthropic warns of ‘existential risks’ in IPO prospectus'; 'Anthropic rolls out second Claude 5.5 model as it builds toward IPO'.

catalysts.title: AI hardware & data‑centre investment build‑out
catalysts.description: Large buybacks, corporate commitments, VC rounds and M&A are fueling a near-term surge in AI infrastructure investment and data‑centre expansion, increasing compute availability.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia launches record $150bn buyback'; 'Samsung Commits $1.0 Billion'; 'AMD to Acquire World Labs'; 'The AI Build‑Out Is Becoming the Biggest Economic Bet'.

catalysts.title: Florida court effort to bar OpenAI model development
catalysts.description: State litigation seeking injunctions against new model development could set legal precedents and impose operational constraints on model releases if successful.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Florida asks court to bar OpenAI from developing new models as part of child harm lawsuit'.

catalysts.title: Acceleration of agentic AI deployment
catalysts.description: Funding rounds, enterprise pushes and new agentic features from major firms indicate rapid rollout of agentic systems across products and enterprises.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'The AI agent revolution has moved a big step closer'; 'Instinct raises $1 billion'; 'Microsoft revamps Copilot'; 'Meta's Muse agent...'.
